summary: AETHER-EVA is an autonomous tactical extravehicular activity (EVA) planning and execution system designed for crewed surface excursions on Mars. Anchored to a candidate human landing site at Arcadia Planitia (38.6556∘N, 190.1000∘E 38.6556∘N, 190.1000∘E), the system delivers an integrated, multi-mission spatial digital twin and astronaut heads-up display (HUD). It eliminates synthetic terrain generation in favor of raw NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) archives, enforcing strict aerospace provenance badges across every layer, metric, and physical model.
details:
A. High-Resolution Tactical 3D Digital Twin

  • Real-Terrain Ingestion: Ingests raw Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) HiRISE stereo topography (DTEEC_061128_2190_061194_2190_A01, Kirk et al. 2008) at 1.0 m posting, aggregated to a 500×500500 \times 500500×500 planning matrix (4.0 m cell resolution, spanning 2.0×2.0 km2.0 \times 2.0\text{ km}2.0×2.0 km).
  • Optical Co-Registration: Draped with true 0.25 m/pixel0.25\text{ m/pixel}0.25 m/pixel monocentric orthorectified imagery (ESP_061128_2190_RED_C_01_ORTHO). Zero procedural noise or random terrain generation.
  • Topographic Context: Accurately models the local elevation depression (datum −3056 m-3056\text{ m}−3056 m, span −3076 m-3076\text{ m}−3076 m to −3036 m-3036\text{ m}−3036 m), selected by NASA for human exploration due to its low atmospheric entry altitude and extensive subsurface sheet ice.

B. Multi-Sensor Layer Dock & Provenance Tracking

Every layer carries an explicit aerospace provenance badge:

  1. Topography (DEM): MEASURED (HiRISE Stereo DTM, 1.0 m native posting).
  2. Orthorectified Optical: MEASURED (HiRISE RED channel, 0.25 m native resolution).
  3. Terrain Slope: DERIVED (Horn 1981 3×33\times 33×3 kernel, >22∘>22^\circ>22∘ hard no-go hazard envelope).
  4. Surface Roughness: DERIVED (Detrended RMS residual elevation variation, 4.0 m).
  5. Clear-Sky Solar Insolation: MODELED (Topographic solar vector at Ls0∘L_s 0^\circLs​0∘).
  6. Topographic Viewshed: DERIVED (3D Bresenham line-of-sight raycasting to Habitat 6 m6\text{ m}6 m mast).
  7. Ionizing Radiation Dosimetry: MEASURED (26.7 μSv/h26.7\,\mu\text{Sv/h}26.7μSv/h Curiosity MSL-RAD surface baseline, Hassler et al. 2014, with ±15%\pm 15\%±15% open-field uncertainty).
  8. Subsurface Radar Ice: MODELED (Subsurface Water Ice Mapping / SHARAD dielectric permittivity proxy).

C. Multi-Objective Tactical Pathfinding

  • Biophysical Locomotion: Governed by NASA's Baseline Values for Exploration (BVAD, NASA/TP-2015-218570), modeling a 220 kg220\text{ kg}220 kg gross suited mass (80 kg80\text{ kg}80 kg crew +140 kg+ 140\text{ kg}+140 kg suit), basal metabolic power of 250 W250\text{ W}250 W, an incline penalty of +8%/deg+8\%/\text{deg}+8%/deg, and an oxygen consumption rate of 0.0525 kg/h0.0525\text{ kg/h}0.0525 kg/h.
    • BALANCED: Nominal multi-factor cost weighting.
    • FASTEST: Minimum traverse time; bypasses conservative detour penalties.
    • LOWEST_DOSE: Prioritizes terrain shadows, crater walls, and depression shielding.
    • BEST_COMMS: Strict line-of-sight optimization maintaining direct RF contact with the habitat.

D. Astronaut Visor AR HUD

  • Optical see-through augmented reality helmet HUD designed for suited crew operations.
  • Displays a conformal pitch ladder, heading tape, waypoint range/bearing reticle, metabolic work rate bar (Watts), suit cooling water reserves, heart rate, and ambient radiation dose rate.

E. Space Weather Contingency & Dynamic Abort Protocol

  • Intercepts Solar Particle Events (SPE CME) and localized dust squalls.
  • Scaled to verified observations from the September 2017 solar event (2.3×2.3\times2.3× dose rate enhancement, Hassler et al. 2018; Zeitlin et al. 2018).
  • Autonomous safe haven resolver calculates terrain viewsheds and recalculates traverse lines toward the nearest natural topographic shelter (14 m Basalt Ridge outcrop, achieving a 42%42\%42% reduction in incident ionizing flux) while enforcing walkback margins (≥0 m\ge 0\text{ m}≥0 m).

F. Interactive Assumptions Panel & Sensitivity Tuning

  • Provides real-time sliders in the Science Specs modal for:
    • Suit Shielding Attenuation (0%−80%0\% - 80\%0%−80%, baseline 40%40\%40%).
    • Open-Field Radiation Uncertainty (±0%−±30%\pm 0\% - \pm 30\%±0%−±30%, baseline ±15%\pm 15\%±15%).
    • Locomotion Slope Limit (12∘−30∘12^\circ - 30^\circ12∘−30∘, baseline 22∘22^\circ22∘).
    • Loose Regolith Speed Factor (0.50×−1.00×0.50\times - 1.00\times0.50×−1.00×, baseline 0.80×0.80\times0.80×).
    • Buddy Separation Envelope (20 m−150 m20\text{ m} - 150\text{ m}20 m−150 m, baseline 50 m50\text{ m}50 m).
    • Operational Walkback Boundary (1000 m−3000 m1000\text{ m} - 3000\text{ m}1000 m−3000 m, baseline 2000 m2000\text{ m}2000 m).
  • Sliders trigger dynamic re-planning in the pathfinding engine, immediately updating traverse distance, duration, metabolic burn, oxygen consumption, and walkback margins.

G. 90-Second Guided Operations Tour

  • Integrated automated sequence demonstrating the tool across 6 distinct phases:
    1. Site Orbit: Candidate landing site selection and HiRISE DTM ingestion.
    2. Data Fusion: Automated cycling through co-registered scientific layers with provenance badges.
    3. Route Presets: Multi-objective A* optimization and real-time factor cost comparisons.
    4. Target POV: High-resolution ground-truth point-of-view inspection at target waypoints.
    5. SPE Hazard: Solar storm alarm, dose rate spike, and safe haven shelter re-route.
    6. Plan Export: Final telemetry synchronization and export verification.
  • Includes playback controls: Pause/Resume (Spacebar), Phase Stepping (← / →), Subtitles/Captions toggle (C), and Exit (ESC). Telemetry reads strictly from live engine state.

H. Flight Telemetry Exporters

  • GeoJSON: Formatted spatial coordinates, waypoint attributes, elevation profiles, and timestamps ready for habitat communication uplink.
  • EVA Cuff Checklist: Formatted printable summary designed for astronaut wrist displays, featuring waypoint turn-by-turn bearings, cumulative distance, consumables budgets, and abort cues.
